claims.text: Adding a small, uniform amount of tungsten to CoCrFeNi will promote in-situ formation of WO3 during sliding.
The resulting WO3 will be stable and lubricious from room temperature to 800 °C.
Tungsten addition will maintain low friction coefficients and wear rates throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting material is an undoped CoCrFeNi matrix with a standard microstructure and native oxide-forming behavior.
A minor weight percentage of tungsten can be alloyed into CoCrFeNi to produce a continuous, thin WO3 tribofilm during sliding.
The proposed operating range is approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under ambient oxidizing conditions.
The tungsten-containing worn surface will develop a continuous and adherent WO3 tribolayer.
The WO3 tribolayer will act as a solid lubricant.
Tungsten dopants preferentially oxidize under sliding conditions to form WO3.
The WO3 film reduces metal-to-metal contact by lowering interfacial shear stress.
The WO3 film prevents severe abrasive wear.
Reduced contact, lower interfacial shear stress, and suppression of abrasive wear will stabilize friction and wear across changing temperatures.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, tungsten-doped CoCrFeNi will have a lower and more stable coefficient of friction at room and elevated temperatures up to 800 °C.
Relative to undoped CoCrFeNi, tungsten-doped CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate at room and elevated temperatures up to 800 °C.
The intervention is expected to be effective in ambient oxidizing atmospheres at moderate sliding speeds and contact loads.
Performance under extreme loads, non-oxidizing conditions, and rapid temperature cycling is undetermined.
The optimum tungsten concentration and long-term stability of the WO3 tribofilm are not known.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction or stabilization of both friction and wear relative to the undoped control, or failure to form a uniform WO3 layer, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The uncertainty field says the optimum tungsten concentration is unknown, while the experiment calls for a fixed, optimized tungsten amount without specifying a prior optimization stage or concentration.
